questions.problem:
An arithmetic sequence $f(n)$ is defined by 

$$
f(n+1)=f(n)-7,\,f(1)=4,\,n\ge 1.
$$

What is the $4$th term of the sequence?
questions.worked_solution:
Starting with the first term $f(1)=4,$ we compute the next terms using the recursive rule until we reach the $4$th term $f(4).$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =4 \\ f(2) & =f(1)-7=4-7=-3 \\ f(3) & =f(2)-7=-3-7=-10 \\ f(4) & =f(3)-7=-10-7=-17\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $4$th term is $f(4)=-17.$

questions.problem:
An arithmetic sequence ${a}_{n}$ is defined by 

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}+15,\,{a}_{1}=0,\,n\ge 1?
$$

The $6$th term of this sequence is{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Starting with the first term ${a}_{1}=0,$ we compute the next terms using the recursive rule until we reach the $6$th term ${a}_{6}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =0 \\ {a}_{2} & ={a}_{1}+15=0+15=15 \\ {a}_{3} & ={a}_{2}+15=15+15=30 \\ {a}_{4} & ={a}_{3}+15=30+15=45 \\ {a}_{5} & ={a}_{4}+15=45+15=60 \\ {a}_{6} & ={a}_{5}+15=60+15=75\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $6$th term is ${a}_{6}=75.$

questions.problem:
What is the recursive formula for the following arithmetic sequence?

$$
-5,\,-2,\,1,\,…
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The recursive formula for an arithmetic sequence with common difference $d$ is

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}+d.
$$

In our case, the common difference is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{2}-{a}_{1} \\  & =-2-(-5) \\  & =-2+5 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the recursive formula for this sequence is

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}+3,\,{a}_{1}=-5,\,n\ge 1\,.
$$

questions.problem:
What is the recursive formula for the following arithmetic sequence?

$$
11,\,7,\,3,\,…
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The recursive formula for an arithmetic sequence with common difference $d$ is

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}+d.
$$

In our case, the common difference is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{2}-{a}_{1} \\  & =7-11 \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the recursive formula for this sequence is

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}-4,\,{a}_{1}=11,\,n\ge 1\,.
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Calculate the fourth term of the sequence

$$
f(n+1) = f(n) -6, \quad f(1) = 1, \quad n\geq 1.
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Starting with the first term $f(1)=1,$ we compute the next terms using the recursive rule until we reach the fourth term $f(4).$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =1 \\ f(2) & =f(1)-6=1-6=-5 \\ f(3) & =f(2)-6=-5-6=-11 \\ f(4) & =f(3)-6=-11-6=-17\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fourth term is $f(4)=-17.$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Finding a Recursive Formula
canonical_examples.problem:
What is the recursive formula for the following arithmetic sequence?

$$
4,\: 9,\: 14,\: \ldots
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The recursive formula for an arithmetic sequence with common difference $d$ is

$$
a_{n+1} =a_n+d.
$$

In our case, the common difference is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{2}-{a}_{1} \\  & =9-4 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the recursive formula for this sequence is

$$
a_{n+1}= a_n + 5, \quad a_1=4, \quad n\geq 1\,.
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Suppose we have the following arithmetic sequence with first term $a_1 = {\color{red}4}$ and common difference  $d={\color{blue}{3}}\mathbin{:}$

$$
{\color{red}{4}},7,10,13,16,\ldots
$$

Each term is ${\color{blue}{3}}$ more than the previous, starting with ${\color{red}{4}}.$ Therefore, we can express this sequence recursively:

$$
a_{n+1} = a_n + {\color{blue}{3}}, \quad a_1 = {\color{red}{4}}, \quad n\geq 1
$$

We can also express the sequence using function notation:

$$
f(n+1) = f(n) + {\color{blue}{3}}, \quad f(1) = {\color{red}{4}}, \quad n\geq 1
$$
